text: Shopping online, you need to pick the best product. Your first stop? The reviews. You just want honest opinions to make a smart choice.
But as you scroll, it's a flood of five-star glowing praise. Every comment sounds perfect, almost too good. Unanimous positivity washes over you.
Your gut says something is off. Are these reviews even real? You suspect a secret team, trying to manipulate your decisions.
The system itself creates this bias. Platforms reward *any* review, but positive ones are easier to write and get amplified. Negative experiences often just fade or are filtered.
The real cost isn't just a bad purchase. It's the constant erosion of trust. You distrust your primary information source, feeling the true story is always hidden.
Next time, you'll still check reviews. But now, you see the invisible incentives and filters shaping that perfect five-star average. You're a smarter shopper.
